   "source": [
    "# Mesh convergence: how fine is fine enough?\n",
    "\n",
    "Every number the eigenmode solver reports is a discretisation of the real cavity, so the\n",
    "first question about any of them is how much of it is the mesh. Here the cavity is a closed\n",
    "metal cylinder, whose TM$_{010}$ frequency is known in closed form, so the error is measured\n",
    "rather than estimated. The answer generalises: reach for the polynomial order before the\n",
    "element size."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "53907cd2",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-09-27T11:18:05.474925Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-09-27T11:18:05.474684Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-09-27T11:18:08.035404Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-09-27T11:18:08.033799Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import os\n",
    "import tempfile\n",
    "\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "from scipy.special import jn_zeros\n",
    "\n",
    "from cavsim2d import Beampipe, Pillbox\n",
    "from cavsim2d.constants import c0\n",
    "from cavsim2d.utils.printing import set_verbose\n",
    "from cavsim2d.utils.style import apply_style, WARM\n",
    "\n",
    "set_verbose(False)\n",
    "apply_style()\n",
    "WORK = tempfile.mkdtemp()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "4b3246bf",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 1. A cylinder with a known answer\n",
    "\n",
    "The TM$_{010}$ frequency of a closed cylinder of radius $R$ is\n",
    "$f = c_0\\,\\chi_{01} / (2\\pi R)$, with $\\chi_{01}=2.405$ the first zero of $J_0$, whatever\n",
    "its length. A `Beampipe` with metal (`'pec'`) end faces is exactly that cylinder."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "0b13d1a0",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-09-27T11:18:08.038695Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-09-27T11:18:08.038259Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-09-27T11:18:08.049416Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-09-27T11:18:08.048703Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "analytic TM010 = 498.880556 MHz\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "data": {
      "text/plain": [
       "Beampipe(name='cylinder', n_cells=1, beampipe='none')"
      ]
     },
     "execution_count": 2,
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "execute_result"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "R, L = 230.0, 200.0                         # mm\n",
    "chi01 = jn_zeros(0, 1)[0]\n",
    "f_analytic = c0 * chi01 / (2 * np.pi * R * 1e-3) * 1e-6   # MHz\n",
    "print(f'analytic TM010 = {f_analytic:.6f} MHz')\n",
    "\n",
    "cav = Beampipe(R, L, ends='pec', name='cylinder')\n",
    "cav.set_workspace(os.path.join(WORK, cav.name))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "749c148c",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 2. Run the convergence sweep\n",
    "\n",
    "Solve the monopole modes at polynomial orders $p = 2$ to $6$. At each order the mesh starts\n",
    "from elements as large as the cylinder allows, `h = 250` mm, a handful of triangles, and is\n",
    "refined adaptively, where the error is largest, until the modes stop moving or the DOF cap\n",
    "is reached. Starting that coarse is what lets the high orders show a convergence curve at\n",
    "all: on a finer first mesh they are already at the precision of the arithmetic."
   ]
  },

   "cell_type": "code",

   "source": [
    "## 3. Convergence of the fundamental\n",
    "\n",
    "The fundamental's relative error against the closed form, against the number of degrees of\n",
    "freedom, one curve per polynomial order. Each triangle is fitted to its curve above the\n",
    "round-off floor and labelled with the slope, the rate at which the error falls as unknowns\n",
    "are added. Theory predicts $p$: the eigenvalue error of order-$p$ elements falls as\n",
    "$h^{2p}$, and in two dimensions the number of unknowns grows as $h^{-2}$. Below about\n",
    "$10^{-14}$ the error has reached the precision of the arithmetic, and the curves go flat."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "id": "6f024abf",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-09-27T11:19:00.964860Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-09-27T11:19:00.964615Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-09-27T11:19:01.449485Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-09-27T11:19:01.448520Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 800x520 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    },
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "fitted rates: {2: 2.0, 3: 2.9, 4: 4.1, 5: 5.1, 6: 5.9}\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "ROUND_OFF = 5e-14\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "def slope_triangle(ax, x, y, color, where, side, width=0.25):\n",
    "    # A right triangle beside a log-log curve, its hypotenuse parallel to a least-squares\n",
    "    # fit of the points above round-off, labelled with the fitted rate. *where* is the\n",
    "    # position along the fitted range (0 to 1) and *side* whether it sits above or below\n",
    "    # the curve.\n",
    "    x, y = np.asarray(x, float), np.asarray(y, float)\n",
    "    keep = y > ROUND_OFF\n",
    "    if keep.sum() < 2:\n",
    "        return None\n",
    "    lx, ly = np.log10(x[keep]), np.log10(y[keep])\n",
    "    k, c = np.polyfit(lx, ly, 1)\n",
    "    x0 = 10 ** (lx.min() + where * (lx.max() - lx.min()))\n",
    "    x1 = x0 * 10 ** width\n",
    "    shift = 4.0 if side == 'above' else 0.25\n",
    "    y0 = 10 ** (c + k * np.log10(x0)) * shift\n",
    "    y1 = y0 * (x1 / x0) ** k\n",
    "    if side == 'above':      # corner top-right: \"1\" along the top, the rate on the right\n",
    "        ax.plot([x0, x1, x1, x0], [y0, y0, y1, y0], color=color, lw=1)\n",
    "        ax.text(np.sqrt(x0 * x1), y0 * 1.5, '1', color=color, ha='center', va='bottom')\n",
    "        ax.text(x1 * 1.06, np.sqrt(y0 * y1), f'{-k:.1f}', color=color, ha='left', va='center')\n",
    "    else:                    # corner bottom-left: the rate on the left, \"1\" along the bottom\n",
    "        ax.plot([x0, x1, x0, x0], [y0, y1, y1, y0], color=color, lw=1)\n",
    "        ax.text(x0 / 1.06, np.sqrt(y0 * y1), f'{-k:.1f}', color=color, ha='right', va='center')\n",
    "        ax.text(np.sqrt(x0 * x1), y1 / 1.5, '1', color=color, ha='center', va='top')\n",
    "    return -k\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "# where each triangle sits, chosen to keep it clear of the neighbouring curves\n",
    "PLACE = {2: (0.5, 'above'), 3: (0.45, 'below'), 4: (0.45, 'below'), 5: (0.3, 'above'),\n",
    "         6: (0.5, 'below')}\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "fund = df[df['mode_index'] == '0-0'].copy()\n",
    "fund['rel_err'] = ((fund['freq [MHz]'] - f_analytic).abs() / f_analytic).clip(lower=1e-16)\n",
    "\n",
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5.2))\n",
    "rates = {}\n",
    "for i, (p, g) in enumerate(fund.groupby('p')):\n",
    "    g = g.sort_values('No of DOFs')\n",
    "    ax.plot(g['No of DOFs'], g['rel_err'], marker='o', ms=5,\n",
    "            color=WARM[i % len(WARM)], label=f'p = {p}')\n",
    "    rates[p] = slope_triangle(ax, g['No of DOFs'], g['rel_err'], WARM[i % len(WARM)],\n",
    "                              *PLACE.get(p, (0.5, 'below')))\n",
    "ax.axhline(ROUND_OFF, color='0.5', lw=0.8, ls=':')\n",
    "ax.set_xscale('log'); ax.set_yscale('log')\n",
    "ax.text(ax.get_xlim()[1], ROUND_OFF * 1.4, 'round-off ', color='0.4', ha='right',\n",
    "        va='bottom', fontsize=9)\n",
    "ax.set_xlabel('degrees of freedom'); ax.set_ylabel('relative error in $f_{010}$')\n",
    "ax.set_title('Adaptive h-refinement at each polynomial order')\n",
    "ax.legend()\n",
    "plt.show()\n",
    "print('fitted rates:', {int(p): round(r, 1) for p, r in rates.items() if r})"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "b7399c3e",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The fitted rates are 2.0, 2.9, 4.1, 5.1 and 5.9 for $p = 2$ to $6$: every order converges at\n",
    "the rate theory predicts for it. Each step up in order adds one to the rate, which is why the\n",
    "higher orders are so much cheaper for the same accuracy. Their curves do not just start\n",
    "lower, they fall faster."
   ]
  },

    "rows = {}\n",
    "for p, g in fund.groupby('p'):\n",
    "    g = g.sort_values('No of DOFs')\n",
    "    rows[p] = {f'DOFs to {tol:.0e}': (int(g.loc[g['rel_err'] <= tol, 'No of DOFs'].min())\n",

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "d24180bc",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "To part-per-billion accuracy ($10^{-9}$), $p = 2$ needs 97 000 DOFs, $p = 3$ 3 000, $p = 4$\n",
    "1 200, $p = 5$ 460 and $p = 6$ 170: some 570 times fewer unknowns from the lowest order to\n",
    "the highest. At $10^{-12}$ the quadratic elements never arrive within the cap, while $p = 6$\n",
    "needs 620 DOFs. Raise the order before refining the mesh."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "5fe8d3ff",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 5. Compare like with like\n",
    "\n",
    "A small change to the geometry is a different cavity, with a different frequency. Put a\n",
    "1 mm hole on the axis of each end face, which is what a `Pillbox` with a 1 mm iris radius\n",
    "is, and solve it on a fine mesh:"
   ]

    "holed.set_workspace(os.path.join(WORK, holed.name))\n",

    "The holes move the frequency by $1.4\\times10^{-7}$, far above the error every order reaches\n",
